```{r}
library(data.table)
# Step 1: List all the text files in the directory
file_list <- list.files(path = "/Users/yihaozhao/Desktop/Cluster Genetic Data Project/data", pattern = "*.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

# Step 2: Define a function to read and clean a single file
read_and_clean_file <- function(file) {
  # Read the file, skipping the first 8 lines, handling tab-separated values
  data <- fread(file, 
                     skip = 8, 
                     sep = "\t", 
                     header = TRUE, 
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
                     fill = Inf,
                     na.strings = "")
  
  # Remove any rows where the first column contains dashed lines
  data <- data[!grepl("^[-]+$", data[, 1]), ]
  
  return(data)
}

# Step 3: Loop over all files and read them into a list of data frames
all_data <- lapply(file_list, read_and_clean_file)

# Step 4: Combine all the data frames into a single data frame
combined_data <- rbindlist(all_data, fill = TRUE)

```

```{r}
# Step 5: Preview the first few rows of the combined data
head(combined_data)

# Step 6: (Optional) Save the combined data to a CSV file if needed
write.csv(combined_data, "combined_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# First, in R download and install Bioconductor using
 
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(version = "3.19")
 
# Then install the GEOquery package:
 
BiocManager::install("GEOquery")
 
# Once installed, load this package
 
library(GEOquery)
 
# Then you can download any pre-processes data posted to Gene Expression Omnibus using
 
drugdata <- getGEO("GSE57815")[[1]]
#methods(class=class(drugdata))
# Aside: The getGEO function will download a list – usually there is only one component in the list as in the case with your data which is why I used the [[1]] notation – you should check if multiple platforms were used and pull the correct item from the list.

 help("ExpressionSet-class")
# The expression data can be extracted using the exprs() extractor function:
 
expression=exprs(drugdata)  # this is G by N (number of genes by number of samples)
print(expression)

# The phenotypic data can be extracted using the pData() extractor function:
 
pData(drugdata)  # this is N by P (number of samples by number of phenotypic variables)

table(pData(drugdata)$"dose:ch1", pData(drugdata)$"time:ch1")

baseline <- drugdata[,pData(drugdata)$"dose:ch1"=="0 mg/kg" & pData(drugdata)$"time:ch1"=="0.25 d"]
exprs(baseline)
dim(exprs(baseline))
pData(baseline)


# select samples : Dose = 0 mg/kg, any duration
baseline2 <- drugdata[, pData(drugdata)$"dose:ch1" == "0 mg/kg"]
x = exprs(baseline2)
dim(exprs(baseline2))
pData(baseline2)

# Similarly measure
xt = t(x) # transpose of data
print(x)
dim(xt)

```

```{r}
# First, in R download and install Bioconductor using
 
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(version = "3.19")
 
# Then install the GEOquery package:
 
BiocManager::install("GEOquery")
```


```{r}
# Once installed, load this package
library(GEOquery)

drugdata <- getGEO("GSE57815")[[1]]
#methods(class=class(drugdata))
# Aside: The getGEO function will download a list – usually there is only one component in the list as in the case with your data which is why I used the [[1]] notation – you should check if multiple platforms were used and pull the correct item from the list.

 help("ExpressionSet-class")
 
# The expression data can be extracted using the exprs() extractor function:
expression=exprs(drugdata)  # this is G by N (number of genes by number of samples)

# The phenotypic data can be extracted using the pData() extractor function:
pData(drugdata)  # this is N by P (number of samples by number of phenotypic variables)

# select samples : Dose = 0 mg/kg, any duration
baseline2 <- drugdata[, pData(drugdata)$"dose:ch1" == "0 mg/kg"]
x = exprs(baseline2)

```


```{r}
#install.packages("matrixStats")
library(matrixStats)

xt = t(x) # transpose of data
sds = colSds(xt) # standard deviations of each rows and columns
boxplot(sds)

# filtering variance > median variance across genes
xt_filter = xt[, sds > median(sds)]
dim(xt_filter)

# Similarity measure: use absolute correlation between genes 
cormat = cor(xt_filter)
dim(d)

# distance
d = 1 - abs(cormat)

# Hierarchical clustering
hclust_complete = hclust(as.dist(d), method = "complete")
plot(hclust_complete)

```
